title: Handoff provisos and fallbacks — 02/25 to 03/11 shift notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal runbook + handoff checklist for the overnight/dawn shift. Mostly broken-in notes and temporary mitigations that I used while triaging the model-serving latency spikes on 2026-03-09. Keep this doc in users for now — will lift to shared drive if we formalize.

Top-level summary (state as of last_mod):
- System: hosted API (api.redwood.ai) fronted by gateway cluster gw-prod-1/2.
- Current risk: intermittent p95 latency spikes to ~1.8s on text-generation endpoints during model reloads and heavy KV-cache churn.
- Active mitigations: route canaries to model-variant: small-v2 during peak windows; disabled auto-reload for large-v1; increased request buffer on gw-prod-2.
- Priority for next shift: verify rollout settings for dedicated customers are not impacted, confirm persistent KV cache warm-up is effective, and add temporary alert for model_kv_cache_miss_rate > 12% for 10m.

Quick checklist (handoff):
- Check Datadog dashboards: "Hosting / API / p95 latency" and "KV cache hit-rate". Link: https://app.datadoghq.com/dashboard/xxxxx
- Confirm canary routing: run `rbac-tool check-route canary-small-v2` (see snippet below).
- Reconcile open incidents: ENGOPS-4123 (latency spike), ENGOPS-4140 (failed quantization job).
- Leave a note in #sre-oncall with summary + timestamp and tag oncall lead (Diego).

Command snippets (copy/paste):
- Verify gateway node health:
  kubectl get nodes -l role=gateway -o wide --context=prod
- Check pods for serving runtime:
  kubectl -n serving-prod get pods -l app=serving-runtime -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,CPU:.spec.containers[*].resources.requests.cpu -w --context=prod
- Force KV cache warm-up (temporary):
  curl -s "https://internal-api/serving/warmup?model=large-v1&shards=all" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
- Roll small canary back to baseline if errors > 0.5%:
  routhandler rollback --route canary-small-v2 --reason "automated rollback per latency policy"

Temporary mitigations we applied (and why):
- Disabled auto-reload on large-v1 (config flag: runtime.auto_reload=false) — reloads were coinciding with KV eviction thrash. This is temporary because hotfix deploys will need reload.
- Small-v2 canary: lighter quantization profile kept CPU and GPU memory stable under burst; used as fallback for unstable large-v1.
- Increased service-level buffer on gw-prod-2: gatekeeper.request_buffer=512 -> 1024 to absorb short surges from retries.

Observations and heuristics I recorded while triaging:
- Pattern: correlated latency spikes with ~30–90s windows where memhigh events occur on a subset of GPU hosts. Those memhigh windows are followed by high KV cache miss rate as the model's embedding shards are rebalanced.
- Useful metric to watch: `serving.runtime.kv_cache_evictions{model=large-v1}` — sudden rises usually predict p95 jump within 60s.
- When rolling back canary, keep watch on `api.request_5xx_rate` — sometimes rollback masks underlying backpressure and a second component (gateway queue growth) will surface.

Known gaps / TODO (next person):
- Add an automated warm-up job triggered after any model reload (ticket: ENGOPS-4158).
- Short-term: add a Datadog alert for `kv_cache_miss_rate > 12%` (10m) as discussed — I left a draft in the alerting repo under /alerts/kv-miss-temp.yaml.
- Longer-term: propose a prefetch strategy for top-50 prefixes per tenant to keep hot paths cached.

Escalation / who to call (order):
1) Oncall lead: Diego Morales (pager)
2) Serving runtime owner: Priya Kapoor (Slack, mobile)
3) SRE infra: Liam O'Neill (pager)
4) Product: Eric Huang (for customer impact comms)

Customer impact note (for handoff):
- No active customer-facing outage as of last check. Some dedicated customers saw higher 95th latency in telemetry — reached out to major affected customers via support channel (Support ticket IDs: SUP-9982, SUP-9987). If we see >2 customer escalations in an hour, open an incident bridge and loop PM.

Rough play-by-play of the 2026-03-09 event (for context):
- 01:12 UTC: p95 jump detected to 1.2s -> 1.8s.
- 01:13 UTC: triage found repeated model reloads on large-v1 on host gpu-eu-9 (log: reload started, OOM avoided by eviction).
- 01:15 UTC: set runtime.auto_reload=false for large-v1 on cluster-serving-eu; started warmup job for large-v1 on other hosts.
- 01:35 UTC: p95 returned to ~650ms after warm-up and canary shift.
- 02:05 UTC: confirmed no steady 5xx spike; closed outage window but left alert rules stricter for next 24h.

Notes-to-self (loose / shorthand):
- If warmup fails repeatedly, check quantization job queue (devops/quant) — ENGOPS-4140 relates.
- Watch for disk-IO on gpu hosts; sometimes KV eviction = disk pressure. `iostat` quick check on host helps.
- When increasing buffer sizes, also check memory tipping — revert if gateway pod restarts increase.

Snippets I left around the repo (for next shift):
- local playbook: /repos/engops/runbooks/kv-cache-temp.md (contains curl endpoints + example warmup payload).
- alert draft: /repos/ops/alerting/kv-miss-temp.yaml (needs review)
- play: PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/987 (small change to auto_reload defaults)

Unresolved questions to raise during overlap:
- Is the memhigh behaviour driven by a third-party collector? (Sana to check host telemetry agent updates)
- Does the dedicated tier routing respect the temporary canary? One customer reported seeing small-v2 responses; confirm tenant routing policy (diego action).

End-of-shift handoff note to incoming oncall (what I'd say in Slack):
- "Incoming: Asha handing off. Watch p95 + kv_cache_evictions for large-v1. Canaries routing to small-v2; auto_reload disabled for large-v1. If you see sustained p95>1.1s for 15m, start bridge and loop Priya. I left temp alerts in Datadog and a draft alert in the alert repo. TAG: ENGOPS-4123."

Appendix: quick cheat table
- Hot metric: serving.runtime.kv_cache_evictions{model=large-v1}
- Quick fix: route to small-v2 -> `routhandler promote --route canary-small-v2` then monitor 5m window
- Warmup endpoint: POST /internal/serving/warmup {model: "large-v1"} (auth required)

----
Random scratch trailing thoughts (feel free to ignore):
- Could we add a rolling cache prefetcher per shard keyed from recent traffic? Not today, but sketching a small service might save 30–60s after reloads.
- If we formalize this, move notes to shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/runbooks/kv-cache-prefetch.md

(End of doc)
